articles.title: NASA Shares Plans to Accelerate Artemis, Return to Moon
articles.description: In an update on Oct. 23, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders shared the agency’s path to returning Americans to the lunar surface in 2028. Agency leadership provided updates on the previously announced acceleration plans for the Artemis program, advancing toward the agency’s Artemis III test flight in 2027 and Artemis IV Moon […]
articles.summary: NASA accelerates its Artemis program to return humans to the Moon, marking a major milestone in lunar exploration and deep space missions.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone nearly 50 years after its launch, even as engineers battle dwindling power and mysterious technical problems. A clever energy-saving maneuver has extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission, while an unexplained 48-hour communications blackout recently gave NASA a scare. On November 18, Voyager 1 will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, making even the simplest round-trip communication take 48 hours.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching a historic milestone of one light-day distance from Earth nearly 50 years after launch, continuing its extraordinary journey as humanity's most distant spacecraft. This achievement celebrates decades of groundbreaking exploration at the edge of our solar system.

articles.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
articles.description: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases used in DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, revealing that key ingredients for life existed in space billions of years ago. The remarkable finding adds to growing evidence from other asteroids and meteorites that these molecules were widespread throughout the early Solar System.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered all five essential DNA and RNA nucleobases in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, confirming that the building blocks of life exist in extraterrestrial materials. This landmark finding strengthens the case that life's chemistry may be widespread throughout the cosmos.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers observed two different types of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart, an unprecedented cosmic event. This discovery provides new insights into some of the universe's most energetic phenomena since the Big Bang.

articles.title: NASA Voyager 1 Is About To Break A Huge Record — Here's When
articles.description: After nearly 50 years, Voyager 1 is about to reach a milestone no spacecraft has ever hit. Once that happens, a simple data exchange will take over two days.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching a historic milestone after nearly 50 years in space that no spacecraft has ever achieved. This remarkable achievement demonstrates humanity's enduring presence in the cosmos.

articles.title: A Mighty Wind Blew Away Gas and Made Early Galaxies Brighter
articles.description: When astronomers looked at photos of the early universe taken by the James Webb Space Telescope, they found something odd: an overabundance of bright galaxies about 400 to 500 million years after the Big Bang. But these galaxies should have been far less common so soon after the Big Bang. Researchers may have figured this out: Powerful ultraviolet (Lyman-alpha) radiation produced by dense clusters of young stars acted like a leaf blower, driving light-blocking gas and dust out of the galaxy and thereby making the galaxies appear brighter.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope reveals that powerful winds in the early universe stripped gas from galaxies, making them unexpectedly bright and reshaping our understanding of galaxy formation.

articles.title: Interstellar Visitor 3I/ATLAS Shows Water Ice Behaves the Same Across Alien Star Systems
articles.description: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. And it just so happens that in the intervening years between the last known interstellar visitor (2I/Borisov in 2019), we got a major upgrade in our observational capabilities with the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). A new paper from a team of researchers led by Dr. Silvia Protopapa of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the Southwest Research Institute, and published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, details JWST’s findings on the water ice content of this most recent visitor from beyond our solar system.
articles.summary: Analysis of interstellar visitor 3I/ATLAS demonstrates that water ice behaves consistently across different star systems, providing insights into the universal nature of cosmic materials.

articles.title: China Unveils Their Plan for a Crewed Moon Landing
articles.description: Yesterday, on November 3rd, the deputy chief designer of China's crewed space program and chief designer of the lunar exploration program (Wang Xiang) unveiled an official statement detailing its [plans for a crewed mission to the Moon](https://english.spacechina.com/n17212/c4744561/content.html).
articles.summary: China announces an ambitious crewed Moon landing program, expanding international efforts to explore and establish a human presence on the lunar surface.

articles.title: A Virtual Lifeless Earth Will Help Scientists Find Life on Exoplanets
articles.description: Researchers have created a model lifeless Earth that couples the atmosphere with interior planetary processes. The model can reproduce Earth's modern habitable state without including life, showing that a planet that appears habitable isn't necessarily inhabited. The tool will be useful when and if the Habitable Worlds Observatory is launched, by helping identify false positives.
articles.summary: Scientists have created a virtual lifeless Earth model that simulates atmospheric and planetary interior processes to help identify biosignatures on distant exoplanets. This innovative tool could revolutionize the search for life beyond our solar system.

articles.title: Webb Space Telescope's little red dots could hold key to first black holes
articles.description: Johns Hopkins researchers searching the expanse of the universe for the existence of the first black holes are zeroing in on little red dots that may hold the key to the theoretical phenomenon.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Johns Hopkins researchers are using the James Webb Space Telescope to identify faint red objects that may represent the universe's first black holes. These discoveries could revolutionize our understanding of black hole formation in the early cosmos.

articles.title: Microbial growth in simulated Mars conditions could guide search for life
articles.description: A new experiment reveals that Earth's microbes can grow in harsh conditions similar to what may exist just below the surface of Mars, suggesting new directions in the search for potential cellular life on the red planet.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New experiments demonstrate that Earth microbes can survive and grow in simulated Martian subsurface conditions, providing crucial insights for the search for life on Mars. This finding could guide future astrobiology missions exploring Mars's habitable zones.

articles.title: NASA navigation experiment shows promise for planetary landings
articles.description: NASA has successfully demonstrated technology designed to help spacecraft autonomously navigate to safe landing sites on the moon and on other planets. An Alta-X drone equipped with the agency's Safe and Precise Landing—Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) guidance, navigation and control payload completed simulated lunar descent and landing maneuvers Aug. 27. The flight took place at Rogers Dry Lake near NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA has successfully demonstrated autonomous navigation technology that enables spacecraft to safely identify and land on optimal sites during planetary landings. This breakthrough promises more precise and safer missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft has captured its first detailed images of the asteroid pair involved in NASA's historic 2022 DART impact experiment. This follow-up mission will provide crucial data on how planetary defense technology can protect Earth from asteroid threats.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover breaks historic record after traveling 28 miles
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, farther than any vehicle has ever driven on another world. Armed with groundbreaking autonomous navigation technology and increasingly advanced driving capabilities, the rover is pushing the boundaries of robotic exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across the Martian surface, surpassing all previous rover distance achievements. This milestone demonstrates the rover's exceptional durability and continued scientific productivity in exploring Mars.

articles.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
articles.description: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.
articles.summary: The IceCube detector has captured ultra-high-energy neutrinos with 10 billion times more energy than solar neutrinos, opening new windows into extreme cosmic phenomena. This achievement enables scientists to study the most energetic events in the universe through these elusive ghost particles.

articles.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
articles.description: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a theoretical loophole in the laws preventing black holes from splitting apart, opening new avenues for understanding black hole physics and behavior.

articles.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
articles.description: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array on Thursday (Nov. 5), wrapping up a multiyear effort to boost the station's power generation by 30%.
articles.summary: Spacewalking astronauts Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk successfully installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array, completing a major upgrade to the International Space Station's power systems.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe bounces back from communications glitch in interstellar space
articles.description: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is back in communication after the 49-year-old spacecraft briefly fell silent last month, during its interstellar-space mission.
articles.summary: NASA's legendary Voyager 1 probe has recovered from a communications glitch in interstellar space, continuing its historic 49-year mission of exploration and discovery.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: Gravitational-wave observations have provided new constraints on supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn, offering insights into black hole formation in the early universe.

articles.title: Figuring out where cosmic neutrinos come from is tricky - radio telescopes could help find where these ‘ghost particles’ originate
articles.description: A researcher just won a Nobel Prize for detecting tiny particles from space. Scientists now want to get better at figuring out where in the cosmos they come from.
articles.summary: Scientists are developing radio telescope techniques to locate the origins of cosmic neutrinos, building on a recent Nobel Prize-winning detection breakthrough. This advancement will help solve the mystery of where these elusive 'ghost particles' originate in space.

articles.title: Possible dwarf planet discovered beyond Pluto
articles.description: Astronomers have found a large icy object beyond Pluto, dubbed 2026 ED138, that could become the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet Read Full Article at RT.com
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a large icy object beyond Pluto designated 2026 ED138 that could be classified as the solar system's sixth dwarf planet. This finding expands our understanding of distant objects in our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: Hubble Learns Galactic History From Stars
articles.description: This Hubble image features the sparkling collection of stars named Messier 30 (M30), also called NGC 7099.
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope captures the stunning star cluster Messier 30, revealing insights into galactic history through the light of ancient stars.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 5 – Enceladus in Silhouette
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 5 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Enceladus in Silhouette […]
articles.summary: An APOD image showcases Saturn's moon Enceladus in silhouette, revealing its mysterious and dynamic nature against the backdrop of space.

articles.title: NASA Announces Ka-Band Satellite Relay Awards for Space Communications
articles.description: NASA selected three companies on Wednesday to perform work to develop Ka-band space relay capability concepts that are compatible with current missions in space, ensuring service continuity for existing spacecraft without requiring modifications to their onboard systems. Through this work, NASA will aim to acquire end-to-end solutions that include space, ground, launch, operations, and integration […]
articles.summary: NASA selects three companies to develop Ka-band space relay capability, advancing communication infrastructure for future space missions.

articles.title: Exoplanets Can't Hide From The JWST's 'Digital Twin'
articles.description: Finding dim exoplanets hidden in the glare of their stars is an ongoing challenge in astronomy. Telescopes use coronagraphs to block out starlight, but even they have their limitations. Researchers have developed a new technique with the JWST that can find dim exoplanets more easily than ever.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope's advanced 'digital twin' technology helps astronomers detect faint exoplanets hidden in stellar glare, enabling breakthrough discoveries in exoplanet research.

articles.title: Game Theory Helps SETI Search for Alien Civilizations
articles.description: SETI can be more effective the more the targets in the search are refined. SETI's newest survey effort uses game theory to inform its search. It's based on the idea that other ETIs would almost certainly use the transit method to detect habitable worlds like Earth.
articles.summary: Game theory principles enhance SETI's search for extraterrestrial civilizations by refining target selection, improving the chances of detecting alien intelligence.

articles.title: Giant Impacts Help Rocky Planets Retain Their Atmospheres
articles.description: For a long time, planetary scientists thought that giant impacts drove a young planet's atmosphere away into space with all the heat they generated. But it turns out the opposite could be true. The mass a young planet gains through a giant impact increases its gravitational hold on its atmosphere.
articles.summary: New research reveals that giant impacts during planetary formation help rocky planets retain their atmospheres, fundamentally changing scientists' understanding of habitability.

articles.title: Connecting artificial intelligence with the tools of astrophysical research
articles.description: Investigating a scientific question is often a complex process. As an astrophysicist studying some of the most energetic phenomena in the universe, I know that finding answers requires much more than reading scientific papers or understanding existing theories. Astrophysical research involves collecting observations, analyzing data, building physical models and comparing their predictions with observations. These tasks require different scientific tools, databases and modeling software and can take considerable time even for experienced researchers.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Researchers are integrating artificial intelligence with astrophysical research tools to tackle complex scientific questions more efficiently. AI is enhancing the ability of astrophysicists to analyze and interpret high-energy cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Earth's slowing spin may have shaped its primordial crust
articles.description: Around 4.5 billion years ago, a planet-sized object collided with the newly formed Earth, throwing out the debris that would later form the moon. The collision left Earth spinning extremely fast, with days lasting just two to five hours. Yet existing models of how Earth's first crust formed and evolved have largely overlooked how the planet's later slowdown might have affected it.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New research suggests Earth's gradually slowing rotation over 4.5 billion years may have influenced the formation and structure of its primordial crust. This discovery reveals previously unknown connections between planetary dynamics and geological processes.

articles.title: European orbiter detects fresh hints of volcanic activity on Mars
articles.description: New evidence from gas seeping above volcanic rifts suggests Mars is not geologically dead deep inside, but merely sleeping. Fresh fissures along the Alba Mons region hint at active spots under the surface, where gases from inside the planet may be making their way up to the surface.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A European orbiter has detected fresh evidence of volcanic gas emissions above Martian rifts, suggesting Mars retains internal geological activity. This discovery hints that Mars may not be geologically dead but rather dormant beneath its surface.
